answer: On reef, every agent must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether it sorts walnut shipments or designs a quill pen. The bond stays locked even if the agent closes its account, so recycling identities cannot free the money early. Creating 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million for a month. The mechanism makes identities costly through committed capital, limiting how many an attacker can maintain at once.
